questions.text: What is the config service, and how do the engines and workers learn that billing_mode changed? Is it polled or pushed, and how long can workers see a stale value?
In both, who decides which engine charges a given invoice, and what stops the old engine from also charging? What does 'charges' mean concretely: a call to the payment provider plus a ledger write?
At the shadow to both and both to new_only moves, what exactly does the person do (a command, a UI click, editing the flag)? Does the system check the gate, or does the person check it by hand?
In freeze, how do both engines stop charging? Is it the rollback record that workers read, and how do you know all in-flight charges have settled before reconcile starts?

In both, the old engine only writes to the shadow store and the new engine charges. During reprocess from new_only, the old engine recomputes skipped invoices. Where do those recomputed invoices go, and how does it know which periods the new engine already charged?
After switch_back, how does the old engine decide a period is 'still due' and charge it? Is that automatic, and when does charging resume relative to clearing the rollback record?

Automatic rollback: who or what measures the charge failure rate over a 10-minute window, and what counts as a charge failure (declines versus system errors)? What if a high rate is just customers' cards declining?
questions.about: Trigger / Rollback from both or new_only

questions.text: What is the 'shadow store', and what happens to the nightly comparison and its results once you leave shadow or both through a rollback?

answers.text: The config service holds billing_mode. Whether workers poll or are pushed changes, and the maximum staleness, are not known. Added as an open question. The per-key ledger and provider check before every charge is the safeguard against a stale worker double-charging.

Each engine reads billing_mode and is only allowed to charge when the mode makes it the charger; in both, only the new engine is. A charge means a payment provider call plus a ledger write, keyed by customer and billing period, checked by key first. Reason: the key makes a second charge impossible even if the mode check fails.

The person checks the gate by hand and changes billing_mode in the config service; the system does not enforce the gate. Reason: the brief says a person always makes forward moves. The exact tool (command or UI) is not decided.

Yes, workers read the rollback record with the flag, and while it exists no engine issues charges. In-flight charges are given time to settle or time out; any still unknown are resolved by reconcile asking the provider by key, so reconcile does not need all of them settled first. Reason: the key lookup makes the outcome knowable.

Recomputed invoices for due periods are held until switch_back and then charged by the old engine. The old engine knows which periods are already charged from the reconcile list (the ledger checked by key) and skips them. Reason: nothing is charged until the mode is back to old_only.

Automatic. Old engine finds due periods by checking the ledger by key. Order is: set billing_mode to old_only, turn the new engine off, then clear the rollback record; charging resumes when the record is gone. Reason: this ensures no engine charges while the mode is still ambiguous.

Not decided who or what measures the rate, and whether card declines count as failures. The brief only says charge failure rate above 2% over any 10 minutes. I would want only system and provider errors counted, but I have no basis from the brief, so it is an open question.

The shadow store holds non-authoritative invoices that are compared but never charged. After a rollback to old_only the nightly comparison stops, past results are kept for audit, and the gate counters reset. Reason: the brief requires gates to start over and the new engine is off after rollback.

questions.text: Who or what carries out freeze, reconcile, reprocess and switch_back: an automated job, or a person following a procedure? What moves it from one step to the next?
What is the 'affected window' that reconcile checks, and how is its start decided for a rollback from both versus from new_only?
When the origin was both, the old engine only wrote invoices to the shadow store. At switch_back, does it charge from those shadow invoices, or recompute them? Why does that origin skip reprocess?
questions.about: Rollback from both, after_reconcile to switch_back

questions.text: How is the pinning of usage events done and who does it? What exactly is pinned, and does it get released afterwards?
questions.about: Rollback steps: reprocess, pin the usage events

questions.text: How does the system know it is day 35? Who records the entry time into new_only, and what makes rollback get refused when the flag still reads new_only?
For a rollback from shadow, is a rollback record still written? What does switch_back actually do there if the old engine is already the charger, and what happens to the new engine's shadow writes?
If a rollback step keeps failing, charging stays paused. Is there any limit on how long customers can go uncharged, and what does on-call do to unblock it?
questions.about: When something fails: A rollback step fails

questions.text: What does 'person decommissions old engine' involve, and is decommissioned a value somewhere or just a state in the diagram?

answers.text: A rollback controller, an automated job, runs the steps. People only trigger a rollback (on-call by hand or the automatic trigger). Each step starts when the previous one succeeds; a failed step stays put and pages on-call. Reason: steps must be resumable and a person should not hand-run a procedure under pressure.

The affected window runs from entry into both up to freeze, for both origins, because the new engine charged for that whole time. It may be wider than strictly needed, but the key lookup makes extra periods harmless. Reason: simple and conservative.

The old engine does not charge from shadow-store invoices, since they are non-authoritative. At switch_back it recomputes any due period from the usage events and charges it, after checking the ledger by key. A rollback from both skips reprocess because the old engine kept computing every invoice in both, so it skipped no events.

The rollback controller pins the usage events from entry into new_only up to now, meaning that range is exempt from the 35-day expiry. The pin is released when the rollback record is cleared. How the usage event log implements the pin is not known; added as an open question.

The entry time is recorded next to billing_mode when the person moves the flag to new_only. A scheduled check marks day 35, and the rollback trigger reads the entry time and refuses once 35 days have passed, even though the flag still reads new_only. Reason: the flag has only four values, so the cutoff needs its own record.

No rollback record is written for a rollback from shadow, because the new engine never charged and nothing needs freezing. switch_back just sets billing_mode to old_only and turns the new engine off, which ends its shadow writes. The shadow store contents are kept for audit. The old engine is already the charger.

The brief gives no limit on how long charging may stay paused, and no override for on-call. The plan assumes on-call fixes the cause and the controller's retry then succeeds. Charges are delayed, never dropped. Added as an open question.

Decommissioned is not a flag value, only an end state in the diagram. It means a person turns off and removes the old engine, which is allowed only from day 35 on. Reason: the flag keeps four values and decommissioning is a one-way operational act, not a billing mode.

questions.text: The pin of usage events happens in reprocess, after freeze and reconcile. Events expire after 35 days. If a rollback from new_only starts on day 34 and freeze or reconcile run past day 35, could the earliest new_only events already be gone before the pin is made? When exactly is the pin taken?
questions.about: Rollback steps: reprocess (pin) / Day 35 arrives during a rollback

questions.text: What makes a mismatch 'unresolved' for the both to new_only gate? Who investigates and marks one resolved, and where is that recorded?
questions.about: Gates / Mismatch (14 days no unresolved mismatch)

questions.text: When a person flips billing_mode from shadow to both (or both to new_only), what happens to billing periods that are partly processed at that moment? Who owns charging a period that the old engine started computing but has not charged yet?
questions.about: Forward moves / What each mode does: both

questions.text: During freeze, how long are in-flight charges given to settle or time out, and what if the provider is slow or down so reconcile cannot get an answer by key? Does reconcile block, or retry in that step?

answers.text: Yes, that was a real hole. The pin is now taken inside freeze, in the same step that writes the rollback record, before reconcile can run. A rollback must be accepted before day 35, and at that moment the earliest new_only events are at most 34 days old, so none are gone. Reason: pinning first closes the window.
The brief says only 'no unresolved mismatches'. I assume a person marks a mismatch resolved after investigating, but who does it and where it is recorded is not known. Added as an open question.

The mode read at charge time decides who charges. A period the previous charger computed but did not charge is charged by the new charger, which finds it by key; periods already in the ledger are skipped. If an old charge is still in flight, the key check prevents a second charge. Reason: the key makes the outcome safe regardless of timing, and staleness of the flag is already an open question.

How long in-flight charges get to settle is not known; added as an open question. The behavior I decided: if the provider cannot answer, reconcile does not guess or skip. It keeps retrying in that step and pages on-call, and charging stays paused so nothing is double charged or dropped.

questions.text: Reconcile produces two lists, charged periods and due-but-uncharged periods. Where are these lists stored? If the controller restarts mid-rollback, does it redo reconcile or reload them?
In new_only the old engine is Stopped. How does it get run for reprocess, and does it write its recomputed invoices anywhere before switch_back?
questions.about: reprocess / What each mode does: new_only

questions.text: While charging is paused, usage events keep arriving and billing periods keep coming due. Who computes invoices for them (new engine, old engine, nobody)? Which engine charges them after switch_back?

What exactly does the trigger do when it is accepted? Does it only start the rollback controller, or also write anything itself? What does the controller do if on-call and the automatic trigger fire at the same moment?

In a rollback from both, periods that the new engine computed but did not charge are 'due'. The old engine recomputes them from usage events. Are the usage events still available for every such period, since only new_only origin pins events?

answers.text: The two lists are saved in the rollback record when reconcile finishes. After a controller restart it reloads the record and resumes at the saved step; it does not redo reconcile. Reason: the record is the durable home for rollback progress.

The controller runs the old engine in a compute-only mode that cannot charge. It writes recomputed invoices to the shadow store as non-authoritative records. Nothing is charged in reprocess. At switch_back the old engine recomputes each due period from the pinned events and charges it. Reason: keeps the rule that nothing is charged from the shadow store. Whether reprocess is needed at all is added as an open question.

Nobody computes or charges while charging is paused. Events keep arriving in the usage log and stay there, since the pause is short against 35-day retention. After switch_back the old engine computes and charges every period still due, found by ledger key. Reason: simplest, and charges are only delayed, never dropped.

Accepting a trigger only creates the rollback record with the origin mode, if none exists, and starts the controller. If a record already exists the trigger is ignored, so simultaneous on-call and automatic triggers give one rollback. This means a shadow rollback now also writes a record, used only as the one-at-a-time guard, and it does not pause charging. Reason: one create-if-absent write is the simplest guard.

That was a real hole. The pin now happens in freeze for both origins. From both it pins everything still in the log, because the uncharged periods are the recent ones. Anything older than 35 days that was already charged is never recomputed. Reason: the uncharged set is recent because the new engine charged continuously in both. Whether this assumption holds when charges were failing for long is not verified.

teachbacks.text:
1. Starting point: the system is in `old_only`. The old engine's billing workers read usage events from the usage event log (events expire after 35 days), compute invoices, charge customers through the payment provider and write the billing ledger (system of record). The mode lives in one global flag, `billing_mode`, held in the config service.

2. Charge mechanics (applies in every mode): a charge is one provider call plus one ledger write for one customer and billing period, keyed by customer+period. Before every charge the key is checked in the ledger and at the provider, so a repeat is not made. Also, each engine reads `billing_mode` right before it charges, and only the engine the mode names as charger may charge.

3. Forward move 1, `old_only` to `shadow`: a person changes the flag in the config service. The new engine now reads the same usage events and writes invoices to the shadow store. It never charges or writes the ledger. The old engine still charges. A nightly comparison job compares the two engines' invoices per customer. Past results are kept, and the gate counters (consecutive days, mismatch rate, invoices compared) are derived from them. New-engine errors in `shadow` are only recorded.

4. Forward move 2, `shadow` to `both`: a person checks the gate by hand (7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared; a day when the comparison did not run does not count). They then change the flag. Now the new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger, and the old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store without charging. A period the old engine computed but did not charge is charged by the new engine, found by key. Periods already in the ledger are skipped by key.

5. Forward move 3, `both` to `new_only`: a person checks the gate by hand (14 days in `both` with no unresolved mismatch, plus Finance sign-off). They change the flag, and the entry time is recorded next to the flag. The old engine stops and the new engine does everything.

6. Day 35: a scheduled check marks day 35 after entry into `new_only`. The flag still reads `new_only`, but rollback is refused from then on. A charge failure only pages on-call. A person may then decommission the old engine (turn it off and remove it). That is not a flag value.

7. Rollback trigger: on-call can start a rollback by hand from `shadow`, `both` or `new_only` (before day 35 in `new_only`). It starts automatically if, in `both` or `new_only`, the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. The trigger creates the rollback record (origin mode, current step, pinned range, two reconcile lists) only if none exists. If one exists, the trigger is ignored, so simultaneous triggers give one rollback. The rollback controller then starts. Workers read the record along with the flag. While it exists no engine issues charges, except when the origin is `shadow`.

8. `freeze` (origin `both` or `new_only`): the controller pins usage events and stores the range in the record. From `new_only` it pins from entry into `new_only` to now. From `both` it pins everything still in the log. Then in-flight charges are given time to settle or time out. Anything still unknown is left for `reconcile`.

9. `reconcile` (origin `both` or `new_only`): for each period in the affected window (entry into `both` up to `freeze`), compare the ledger with the provider by key. Unknown outcomes are resolved by asking the provider, and a charge is made only if the provider reports none. If the provider is slow or down, it keeps retrying and pages on-call, and never guesses. It saves two lists in the record: periods already charged (never charge again) and periods due but uncharged.

10. `reprocess` (origin `new_only` only): the old engine runs in a compute-only mode that cannot charge. It recomputes the invoices it skipped from the pinned events and writes them to the shadow store, skipping periods on the already-charged list. From `both` this step is skipped.

11. `switch_back`: set `billing_mode` to `old_only`, turn the new engine off, and only then clear the record. Clearing the record releases the pin and resumes charging. The old engine finds what is still due by ledger key, recomputes each due period from usage events and charges it. It never charges from shadow-store invoices. Periods that came due during the pause were computed by nobody, so the old engine computes and charges them now from events still in the log.

12. Rollback from `shadow`: the new engine never charged, so there is no `freeze`, `reconcile` or `reprocess`. `switch_back` sets `old_only`, turns the new engine off (ending its shadow writes) and clears the record. The shadow store is kept for audit.

13. After rollback: the nightly comparison stops, and all gates and counters reset. The next forward move must be `old_only` to `shadow`, with the 7-day count at zero.

14. Failures in a rollback: the controller moves to the next step only when a step succeeds. If a step fails it stays in that step with charging paused, keeps retrying and pages on-call. Due charges wait and are not dropped. If the controller restarts, it reloads the record and resumes at the saved step with the saved lists. If day 35 arrives mid-rollback, the rollback still finishes, because events were pinned at the start of `freeze`.
gaps: How workers learn of a change to the flag or the rollback record (poll or push) and how stale a value can be is unknown, so I cannot say exactly when each engine stops or starts charging after a flag change or record creation.
How long in-flight charges get to settle or time out in `freeze` is not decided, so I cannot say when `freeze` moves on to `reconcile`.
What measures the charge failure rate, and whether card declines count, is unknown, so I cannot say exactly what fires the automatic trigger.
What tool a person uses to change the flag is not decided, and whether anything checks the gate is unclear (assumed to be by hand), so I cannot say how a forward move is carried out or guarded.
How the pin is actually done in the usage event log is unknown.
Who marks a mismatch resolved, and where that is recorded, is unknown, so I cannot say how the `both` to `new_only` gate is evaluated.
Whether a new unresolved mismatch restarts the 14-day count is not settled (the document only assumes it does).
Whether there is a limit on how long charging may stay paused, and whether on-call can skip or cancel a rollback step or the rollback, is unknown.
How the controller turns the new engine off, and how the old engine is put into compute-only mode, is not described.
How the controller detects that a step has succeeded or failed is not described.
Whether a rollback must also finish before day 35, and what happens in the gap between accepting the trigger and the pin, is only partly answered.
In a rollback from `both`, whether the pin covers all uncharged periods if charges failed for a long time is unverified.
